title: EIN Without an SSN or ITIN in 2026: The Exact Process Non-US Residents Must Follow to Get a US Tax ID for Their LLC
content:
# EIN Without an SSN or ITIN in 2026: The Exact Process Non-US Residents Must Follow to Get a US Tax ID for Their LLC

Getting an EIN as a foreign national is not complicated, but the process is specific. One wrong step means delays, rejections, or being locked out of opening a U.S. bank account for months.

---

## Why You Need an EIN Before Almost Everything Else

An Employer Identification Number (EIN) is your LLC's federal tax ID. Without it, you cannot open a U.S. business bank account, set up Stripe or PayPal, file taxes, or hire contractors. It is the foundation of operating a real U.S. business remotely.

The good news: you do not need a Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) to get one. The IRS has a specific process for foreign nationals, and it works reliably in 2026.

---

## The Only Method That Works for Non-Residents in 2026

The IRS online EIN application is restricted to individuals with a U.S. SSN or ITIN. That route is closed to you.

Your only official option is **Form SS-4**, submitted by one of these three methods:

| Method | Processing Time | Cost |
|--------|----------------|------|
| Fax (international) | Approximately 4 business days | Free |
| Mail (international) | 4 to 5 weeks | Free |
| Phone (IRS international line) | Same day | Free |

> **Note:** The phone method is the fastest and most underused option. The IRS International EIN line is +1 (267) 941-1099. It operates Monday to Friday, 6am to 11pm Eastern Time. You must be an authorized member of the LLC to call.

---

## Step-by-Step: How to Complete and Submit Form SS-4

### Step 1: Form Your LLC First

You must have a registered LLC before applying for an EIN. The EIN is issued to a legal entity, so your LLC must already exist in your chosen state. If you have not done this yet, read our [LLC Guide](/llc-guide) before continuing.

### Step 2: Download and Fill Out Form SS-4

Get the current version from IRS.gov. Key fields to complete correctly:

- **Line 1:** Legal name of your LLC exactly as registered with the state
- **Line 7a:** Enter your own name as the responsible party (this is you, the foreign owner)
- **Line 7b:** Enter "Foreign" here since you have no SSN or ITIN
- **Line 9a:** Check "Limited liability company" and enter the number of members
- **Line 10:** Select the reason (starting a new business is most common)
- **Line 11:** Enter the date the LLC was legally formed
- **Line 13:** Enter "N/A" for closing month if you are a single-member LLC defaulting to disregarded entity status

### Step 3: Submit via Fax or Phone

**By Fax:** Send the completed SS-4 to the IRS at +1 (855) 641-6935 (from inside the U.S.) or +1 (304) 707-9471 (from outside the U.S.). Keep your confirmation sheet.

**By Phone:** Call the international line, confirm your identity, and read out the SS-4 information. The agent will issue your EIN verbally on the call and you can request a confirmation letter.

> **Note:** Always request the EIN confirmation letter (CP 575) during your call or note it on your fax cover sheet. Banks and payment processors frequently ask for this document, not just the number itself.

---

## Common Mistakes That Cause Rejections

- **Wrong responsible party information:** The responsible party must be a real individual, not the LLC itself.
- **Mismatched LLC name:** The name on SS-4 must match exactly what is on your state formation documents. Abbreviations and punctuation matter.
- **Calling outside IRS hours:** The international line has limited hours. Call attempts outside Monday to Friday, 6am to 11pm Eastern will not connect to an agent.
- **Not having your LLC documents ready:** On a phone call, the agent may ask for your state registration date, the state of formation, and your LLC's principal business activity. Have these in front of you.

---

## What Happens After You Get Your EIN

Once you have your EIN and the CP 575 letter, you are ready to:

1. Open a U.S. business bank account (Mercury, Relay, or a traditional bank)
2. Set up Stripe, PayPal, or Wise for payment processing
3. File annual reports and handle federal tax obligations

Processing your EIN correctly the first time saves weeks of back-and-forth. Most non-residents who face delays made an error on Line 7b or called outside of business hours.

---

## Ready to Set Up Your U.S. Business the Right Way?

The EIN is just one piece of the puzzle. If you want a step-by-step breakdown of forming an LLC, getting your EIN, opening a bank account, and staying compliant as a non-resident, visit our [Start Here](/start-here) page.
